title: WPMS/1409/2020 of MOHD ASLAM Vs CHIEF ENGINEER LEVEL-I IRRIGATION DEPARTMENT OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1409 of 2020
Mohd. Aslam ...Petitioner
Vs.
Chief Engineer Level-I Irrigation Department
of Uttarakhand and others ...Respondents
Advocate: Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. Sudhir Singh, Standing Counsel for the State
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
The petitioner is a contractor, to whom various work orders
are said to have been issued by the respondents in his favour for
performing various works as assigned in the work orders which are
appended with the writ petition.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the second
party who was the signatories to the agreement or the work order,
had already recommended the payment of the bill of the amount
claimed by the petitioner by virtue of the relief clause of the writ
petition, after the alleged satisfactory completion of his work. The
contention of the petitioner is that since there is no dispute as such as
of now that the petitioner has not completed his work and hence in
the absence of there being any dispute as such regards nature of work
and there being no dispute pertaining to the entitlement of the
petitioner to get an amount paid for, he has filed the present writ
petition for a direction by way of a writ of mandamus.
3. In the writ petition, the petitioner had annexed various work
orders and for the purpose of present judgement, one of the clause
'8' of the work order which is common in all the work orders issued
is quoted hereunder:-
"8. Every dispute, difference or question which may at
any time, during the continuance of this agreement of
after its termination from any cause whatsoever arise
between the parties hereto or any person claiming under
them touching or arising out or in respect of the same of
the subject matter thereof shall be referred to the
arbitration of the Executive Engineer of the and the
decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on
the parties."

2
4. As per the said clause, it provide that wherever there is (a)
dispute; (b) difference or (c) the question, which may at any time
arise.
5. During the continuance of agreement or after its termination,
the matter would be referred to an Arbitrator as described therein.
The reference of dispute or a determination to be made by an
arbitrator, as is contemplated under clause 8 is at both the stages
during the continuance of the agreement when the work is being
performed by the contractor or after the termination of the contract;
the termination herein would mean the cancellation of the work order
or the termination of work order as a consequence of completion of
work. It is the second aspect which is being sought to be argued that
the termination herein would mean that since the petitioner has
completed the work and there is no controversy with regard to the
payment, the writ petition would be amenable under Article 226 of
the Constitution of India.
6. The matter was argued on number of occasions, this Court
while asking the petitioner to place on record any document,
correspondence, bill or communication which was ever made by the
respondents, where they have admitted their liability, with regard to
the claim of payment of money raised by the petitioner in the writ
petition in relation to the work performed by him under the work
orders issued in his favour.
7. The petitioner has filed a supplementary affidavit and in the
supplementary affidavit, he has annexed various bills which were
endorsed by the respondents, which petitioner contends that they
determined that it was admitted amount payable to the petitioner
which he would be otherwise entitled to receive from the
respondents. But this Court cannot be ignorant of the communication
annexed as annexure 2 to the supplementary affidavit dated
24.07.2020, which is a letter written by the Chief Engineer, Haridwar
to the Executive Engineer, Haridwar, soliciting his appropriate action
as a consequence thereto, which was taken as a consequence of the

3
legal notice which was served by the petitioner through his counsel
dated 23.07.2020 on the respondent(s) wherein the Chief Engineer
had directed the competent officer to take an action lest failing which
the Chief Engineer has warned them that in case if any proceedings
are taken they would be responsible for any judicial proceedings, if it
is drawn by the petitioner against the department.
8. This communication dated 24.07.2020 and the notices issued
by the petitioner on 23.07.2020, itself would mean that there happens
to be some apparent controversy pertaining to the entitlement and the
liability of the respondent to remit the amount and that is why the
need arose for the petitioner to serve a legal notice. In such an
eventuality, I am of the view that once the claim has been sought to
be enforced by the petitioner after issuance of legal notice dated
23.07.2020, it would amount to that it was not a claim which was
admitted by the respondent, which could be directed to be paid by
issuance of a writ of mandamus. Hence since being conscious of the
conditions of the work order, which is equally binding on the
petitioner, since the petitioner himself has agreed upon a forum to
decide the dispute under clause 8 of the work order, hence the writ
petition is dismissed on that count of availability of Arbitration
clause, with liberty open to the petitioner to approach and invoke
clause 8 of the work order by approaching before an arbitrator for
redressal of his grievance.
9. Subject to the aforesaid liberty, the writ petition lacks merits
and the same is hereby dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 22.09.2020
Mahinder/
